Indian Navy kicks off Exercise Varuna along with France Navy off Goa

By:Financial Express - 3 May,2019

Short Detail

The 17th edition of the Indo-French bilateral naval exercise Varuna 19.1 is underway and as part of the Harbour phase crews onboard the ships will have interaction and discussions about the wide spectrum of the exercises and maritime security.

This year’s Ex Varuna is not only complex but is also focused on carrier operations and Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) training and Mutual Logistics Support Agreement (MLSA) will be in force too which has been inked between India and France.

The main idea behind this drill is to develop the ability between the navies of both countries Source:News Bharati

From the Indian side aircraft carrier INS Vikramaditya, destroyer INS Mumbai, the Teg-class frigate, INS Tarkash, the Shishumar- class the submarine, INS Shankul, and the Deepak- class fleet tanker, INS Deepak are participating.

Aircraft carrier FNS Charles de Gaulle, two destroyers, FNS Forbin and FNS Provence, the frigate FNS Latouche-Treville, the tanker FNS Marne and a nuclear submarine have come from France.

The 2nd part of the naval exercise, Varuna 19.2, will be held at May-end in Djibouti.

PUTIN SIGNS LAW TO HELP RUSSIA HAVE 'SOVEREIGN INTERNET' THAT CAN BE DISCONNECTED AT WILL

By:Firstpost - 2 May,2019

Short Detail

Russian President Vladimir Putin has signed into law a measure that expands government control over the internet and which critics say will lead to widespread censorship. Putin is expecting that this law will give Russia a 'sovereign internet' which Kremlin can disconnect from the global internet at will.

Demonstrators at an opposition rally in Moscow last month protest against the bill about sovereign RuNet and censorship on the Internet. Source:rferl.org

The law, requires internet providers to install equipment to route Russian internet traffic through servers in the country. Proponents said it is a defence measure in case the United States or other hostile powers cut off the internet for Russia.

Roskomnadzor’s chief (Roskomnadzor is Russia’s chief media regulator), Aleksandr Zharov, notified that the measures would also target the Telegram app widely used by Russians.

The text of the law was published on 1st May 2019 and will come into effect after November.

Goldman Prize Honors Environmental Activists Who Risk Their Lives

By:Voice of America - 1 May,2019

Short Detail

The Goldman Environmental Foundation honoured 6 recipients of the 2019 with the world’s eminent award for grassroots environmental activists, the Goldman Environmental Prize.The Goldman Environmental Prize is also known as Green Nobel Prize and awards a cash prize of $200,000.

In 2019, Goldman Environmental Prize honoured 6 grassroots environmental activists for their exemplary work in protecting the nature Source:commondreams.org

Recipient

  • Bayarjargal Agvaantseren from Mongolia:

    Bayarjargal Agvaantseren helped to create the 1.8 million-acre Tost Tosonbumba Nature Reserve (in the South Gobi Desert) which is a critical habitat for the vulnerable snow leopard. She also persuaded the Mongolian government to take actions against mining within.

  • Alfred Brownell from Liberia:

    Environmental lawyer Alfred Brownell stopped the clear-cutting of Liberia’s tropical forests by palm oil plantation developers. His effective campaign helped to save 5,13,500 acres of primary forest. He was under violent threats during the entire noble campaign and now, for his safety, he is living in temporary exile in the United States.

  • Ana Colovic Lesoska from North Macedonia:

    Alberto Curamil (jailed in 2018 due to his environmental activism) led his Mapuche community to stop the building of 2 hydroelectric projects on the Cautín River in Chile. The projects would have diverted hundreds of millions of gallons of water each day and harmed the ecosystem drastically by worsening drought conditions.

  • Jacqueline Evans from Cook Islands:

    Jacqueline Evans organized a 5-year campaign to protect the Cook Islands’ marine biodiversity. Because of her persistency in activism, the Cook Islands passed a new law to create ‘Marae Moana’ on 13 July 2017 (a multiple-use marine protected area created), to sustainably manage and preserve 763,000 square miles of the nation’s marine territory by creating marine protected areas around all 15 islands.

  • Linda Garcia from United States:

    Linda Garcia prevented North America’s largest oil terminal, Tesoro Savage oil export terminal, from being constructed in Vancouver, Washington, thus curbing the flow of 11 million gallons of crude oil per day from North Dakota to Washington.

    • Source:Wikipedia

    UK Parliament declares 'climate emergency'

    By:CNN International - 1 May,2019

    Short Detail

    Lawmakers in the UK Parliament have declared "an environment and climate emergency," making it the first country in the world to do so, according to the opposition Labour Party.

    The UK Parliament becomes the first national government to pass an Environment and Climate Emergency Source:The Labour Party,Twitter Handle

    The declaration was preceded by a visit by teenage activist Greta Thunberg (to the Parliament), the feature of David Attenborough’s documentary movie titled ‘Climate Change: The Facts’ and the 11-days of constant protest by an environmental group ‘Extinction Rebellion‘.

    The decision of emergency in Parliament caters to national reductions and investment in the reduction of carbon emissions and saving the planet.

    Compared to its 1990 levels, UK (United Kingdom) was later legally committed to an 80% reduction in carbon emissions by 2050 and recently featured as 1 of 18 developed economies to decrease CO2(carbon dioxide) emissions in the last 10 years.

    By:The Hindu - 28 April,2019(IST)

    Short Detail

    The research team from IIT Madras has used a multi-lingual Optical Character Recognition (OCR) scheme to develop a method for reading documents in Bharati script.The Bharati script is a conglomeration of 9 Indian languages, namely, Devnagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Oriya, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Tamil.

    The researchers have also developed a finger-spelling method that can be used by hearing-impaired persons to generate sign language, in collaboration with TCS Mumbai.

    Jamia team develops ultrasensitive quantum thermometer

    By:The Hindu - 28 April,2019(IST)

    Short Detail

    Researchers at Jamia Millia Islamia, New Delhi, have developed an ultrasensitive quantum thermometer by using graphene quantum dots. It can precisely measure a wide range of temperature from 27 degree C to –196 degree C.
